artists.biography:
Crippled Black Phoenix is a rock supergroup from the United Kingdom. Several musicians have contributed to Crippled Black Phoenix's albums and play with them during their live shows.

Members of the band used to play in other bands (including Iron Monkey, Gonga, Mogwai, Electric Wizard and others). In 2004, Justin Greaves began recording primitive sounds he had in mind for years. He was encouraged by Dominic Aitchison, and their ideas would lay the backbone for Crippled Black Phoenix.
Although originally having an unorthodox start, since all the band members were part of and busy with other projects at the time of the band's founding, Crippled Black Phoenix remained committed to staying together and forged their sound. The band writes what they call "endtime ballads," signifying both the slightly macabre nature of their songs and their unusual blend of styles as the final evolution in music. This blend has led to them being called everything from stoner-prog to freak-folk to doom.

Crippled Black Phoenix have made live shows a focus and have performed in unusual venues, using Victorian-era instruments in tandem with more modern instruments.

perplexity.description:
Crippled Black Phoenix's Bronze, released in 2016 on Season of Mist, is a genre-defying rock album that blends post-rock, progressive rock, and classic hard rock with a distinct 1970s influence. The album features a dark, moody atmosphere throughout, combining oppressive, sludgy riffs reminiscent of Black Sabbath with introspective, somber passages and experimental soundscapes. Tracks like "Dead Imperial Bastard" and "Deviant Burials" set the tone with their dramatic intensity, while quieter moments such as "Goodbye Then" showcase the band's ability to build claustrophobic, atmospheric tension. The album also includes a notable cover of Joe Walsh's "Turn to Stone," featuring guest vocals from Arvid Jonsson of Greenleaf, highlighting the band's eclectic approach and musical range.

Bronze stands as a pivotal release in Crippled Black Phoenix's discography, marking their debut on Season of Mist and further establishing their reputation for ambitious, multi-faceted rock music. Led by multi-instrumentalist Justin Greaves, the band's sound on this album is both enigmatic and expansive, incorporating elements of psychedelic, space, and doom rock. The album received positive critical attention for its originality and depth, with reviewers praising its dark, dramatic character and the seamless integration of diverse musical styles. While not a commercial blockbuster, Bronze solidified Crippled Black Phoenix's status as a unique force in the progressive and dark rock scenes.
